title: Onboarding eval: anomaly root-cause atlas and intervention notes
content:
Executive summary:

This note documents a complementary analysis to the onboarding eval for model X-3.2q. Instead of conventional cluster labels (hallucination/regression), we built an "anomaly atlas" — a hierarchical taxonomy of signal slices derived from per-example metrics, tokenization traces, and prompt interaction patterns. The goal is to produce high-precision mitigations that target mechanistic root causes and are cheap to experiment with in Hosted + Dedicated flows.

Quick takeaways:
- We identified 7 reproducible anomaly families (atlas groups) across 6k failing examples.
- Three clusters are clearly upstream (input processing / tokenization / context truncation), two are model decoding quirks, one is prompt-composition interaction, and one appears to be dataset label noise surfacing under new model priors.
- Early low-effort mitigations (preprocessors, prompt canonicalizers, decoding constraints) recover ~42% of infractions with minimal perf cost; targeted reranker fallback regains another ~16%.

Data and signals used:
- onboarding eval promptset (6,200 failing examples flagged by automated QA harness)
- per-token logprobs and decoder beam traces from runtime logs
- tokenizer boundary maps (byte offsets) aligned to reference labels
- context eviction metrics (KV-cache eviction counts for long-history prompts)
- secondary metrics: repetition score, entity-merge score, and classifier-based hallucination score

Method overview:
1) Feature extraction: produced numeric features for each example (token-split artifacts, low-confidence spans, context-eviction count, prefix mismatch score).
2) Hierarchical clustering: agglomerative clustering with a custom distance that weights token-boundary anomalies and low-confidence entity spans higher.
3) Manual labeling pass: 2 engineers reviewed cluster exemplars to give semantic names and hypothesize mechanisms.
4) Validation: small batch experiments for each mitigation on 500 holdout failing examples.

Atlas groups (short names + description):
1) token-split-label-leak: label tokens get fragmented across token boundaries causing partial-match heuristics to fail. Typical manifest: truncated entity tokens, classifier misfires when reference string spans a soft split.
2) context-eviction-chaining: long multi-turn prompts cause older instructions to be evicted from KV cache; subsequent generations ignore earlier constraints and drift style/format.
3) repetition-seed-loop: model falls into a short-loop repetition after producing a high-prob prefix; common when decoding temperature is raised and length penalty is low.
4) entity-merge-hallucination: model invents merged entities (two real entities concatenated) likely due to co-occurrence priors changed in X-3.2q.
5) prompt-composition-interference: composed prompts that mix system/assistant/user fragments in certain orders trigger inverted completions (assistant echoes instructions as content).
6) soft-label-noise-amplification: noisy labels in onboarding dataset that were previously tolerated are amplified by the new model’s stronger priors (overconfident interpolation), exposing ground-truth conflicts.
7) trailing-punctuation-sensitivity: outputs differ dramatically when reference prompts have or lack trailing punctuation/whitespace (tokenizer-sensitive).

Per-cluster analysis and evidence (summary):
- token-split-label-leak: 1,120 examples. Evidence: 78% have label boundaries aligned to tokenizer splits; classifier score crosses pass/fail on adding a single byte-boundary-joining char. Example prompt: "Extract the code: ABC-1234" -> model returns "ABC-12". Repro on CPU runtime by forcing GPT-like greedy decode.
- context-eviction-chaining: 930 examples. Evidence: KV-eviction count correlates with alignment loss; explicit prefix caching prevents drift in 64% of heldout cases.
- repetition-seed-loop: 710 examples. Evidence: logprob curves show a sharp plateau; constraining sampling (top-p clamp + min length penalty) breaks the loop.
- entity-merge-hallucination: 1,010 examples. Evidence: merged tokens frequently have high pairwise PMI in training snapshots and co-occur in fine-tune samples. Simple reranker that penalizes unseen concatenations recovers 41% of these.
- prompt-composition-interference: 980 examples. Evidence: ordering of assistant/user blocks changed expected role handling. Changing the canonical prompt envelope (move explicit "System:" line to top) recovers 52%.
- soft-label-noise-amplification: 740 examples. Evidence: manual label audit for 120 samples showed ~55% had ambiguous or borderline labels; model amplified minority interpretations. Re-labeling and fine-tune suggested as long-term fix.
- trailing-punctuation-sensitivity: 710 examples. Evidence: whitespace and punctuation differences flip outputs; normalizing trailing punctuation before scoring recovers 67% of these.

Mitigation proposals (ranked cheap->expensive):
A) Preprocessor canonicalizer (cheap): normalize trailing punctuation/whitespace, join common token fragments (heuristic join on hyphenated IDs), and collapse multi-space. This is non-invasive and can be tested in Hosted route within days. Expected recovery: ~22% overall, concentrated in token-split and trailing-punct clusters.
B) Prefix pinning / sticky cache (cheap-medium): for routes where user provides an explicit system instruction that must persist, implement sticky-prefix caching in the runtime to prevent eviction for specified token counts. Expected recovery: addresses ~64% of context-eviction cases; cost: modest memory increase.
C) Prompt-envelope rewrite (cheap): canonicalize multi-block prompts into a single, ordered envelope that enforces System->User->Assistant ordering. Expected recovery: ~50% of composition-interference. Low risk.
D) Decoding guardrails (cheap): add repetition penalties and dynamic top-p clamps on prompts showing plateaued logprob traces. This reduces repetition-loop and some hallucination variants with negligible latency impact.
E) Reranker fallback (medium): lightweight reranker that detects merged-entity patterns (n-gram concatenation heuristics) and falls back to a constrained decoding or alternate model. Recover ~40% of entity-merge cases but adds a second pass latency on flagged examples.
F) Targeted relabel + micro-finetune (expensive): curate clear labels for ambiguous dataset slices and run a focused fine-tune/LoRA pass. Expected to substantially improve soft-label-noise-amplification cluster but requires labeling effort and a retrain window.
G) Tokenizer tweaks (expensive/fragile): evaluate alternative token splits for high-signal domains (IDs, codes). This is brittle across languages and may break other behavior — suggested only if canonicalizer fails.

Validation experiments run (summary):
- Canonicalizer pilot (n=500 failure holdout): 110 recovered, mostly token-split + trailing-punct.
- Sticky-prefix simulation (n=300): 72 recovered context-eviction; memory overhead simulated at +12% for those pools.
- Decoding guardrails A/B (n=600): repetition incidents dropped by 81% with small increase in average token per reply (0.9 tokens).
- Reranker small-A/B (n=210): latency +180ms on reranked examples; conversion to pass for flagged samples = 38%.

Open questions / risks:
- Reranker durability: new merged-entity constructions may appear over time; a heuristic reranker will need to be stocked with examples and continuously updated.
- Fine-tune cost vs gains: for some customers the micro-fine-tune path may be preferable (enterprise SLAs), but we need a clear labeling budget and time window.
- Cross-route leakage: prefix pinning for Dedicated customers must be opt-in; we observed a small class of examples where sticky prefix prevented intended system updates mid-session.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Aisha: roll canonicalizer as a per-route opt-in patch in Hosted (ETA 2 weeks) — JIRA JIRA-ML-887.
- Marco: prototype sticky-prefix in staging and measure eviction vs mem overhead (ETA 3 weeks) — linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/191.
- Lena: prepare 120-sample relabel batch and estimate labeling hours for micro-finetune (ETA 1 week).
- Noah: build reranker lightweight rule-set and run latency profile (ETA 3 weeks).

Notes to reviewers:
- This atlas is intentionally conservative in naming; clusters should be seen as diagnostic surfaces not final bug categories.
- If you re-run the hierarchical clustering code, seed=42 gives reproducible clusters; distance weights were set to emphasize token-boundary features (details in linked Confluence).
- Prioritize canonicalizer + decoding guardrails for immediate rollout; reserve tokenizer changes for longer-term evaluation.

Appendix (examples):
- token-split-label-leak example: prompt: "Order ID: ZX-99-AB12. Return reason: ..." label: "ZX-99-AB12"; model output: "ZX-99-AB1". Tokenizer split occurs at last char.
- prompt-composition-interference example: user bundles a system instruction mid-prompt; model echoes instruction text as answer. Canonicalizer rewrite to force system first fixes.

If you want the raw notebook, clustering artifacts, or input lists for any cluster, ping me or see CONFLUENCE-3214.
